gallery.title: File:Paardekraalmonument, oosplaket, Krugersdorp.jpg
gallery.description: Paardekraal, east facet, that reads:1837 A.H. Potgieter went with his company to the region now known as the Orange Free State, where on the south side of the Vaal river he was unexpectedly attacked by Mzilikazi who from the region north of the Vaal river, now district Marico, without provocation thereto launched this attack on him, and carried off white children besides all their livestock. Mzilikazi was in a quest to recover the children and livestock pursued and defeated by Potgieter and his Commandos. Mzilikazi fled from the country.1839 Potgieter trekked north traversing the Vaal river, found the land completely desolate and took possession of it and the basis was established for the existence of the Republic.

gallery.filename: General Jacobus Philippus Snyman at Mafeking.png
gallery.title: File:General Jacobus Philippus Snyman at Mafeking.png
gallery.description: General J.P. Snyman with a group of men and soldiers in front of a covered military wagon, during the South African Campaign. The back of the photo is labelled General Snyman. Commandant of the Transvaal State-Artillery, Lieutenant-Colonel S.P.E. Trichard (*23.01.1847 Ohrigstad) (+Oct.1907 Kenya) is seated in the center, holding his rifle with his left-hand, wearing a top-hat.

gallery.filename: General J.P. Snyman with General Piet Cronje and Captain of the Transvaal State-Artillery, P.J. van der Merwe.png
gallery.title: File:General J.P. Snyman with General Piet Cronje and Captain of the Transvaal State-Artillery, P.J. van der Merwe.png
gallery.description: Taken in the early days of the siege, shows General Piet Cronje (afterwards captured at Paardeberg), whip in hand, standing at the breech of the 94-pounder "Long Tom" nicknamed "Creechy" (abbreviation for Marguerite), or "Creaky," which had frequent duels with the little Nordenfeldt. On his right, pipe in mouth, is Assistant General J.P. Snyman, and on his left is Captain of the Transvaal State-Artillery, P.J. van der Merwe.
